experiment: Targeted repeated-process variance check after selective exact-scale normalization

method.before: Base Decimal/coercion patch plus high-scale whole/remainder fallback and filter/projection dependency fix.
method.after: Same candidate plus selective exact-scale normalization at 526cb3a. No ROUND patch or fused UDF.
method.case_order: Rotate the listed three cases left by pass index modulo 3.
method.perf_control: perf stat --delay=-1 --control=fifo:DIR/control,DIR/ack; enable after setup and two warmups, disable after nine executions. Acknowledgements are checked.
method.counter_scope: Aggregate of nine measured executions plus control handshake and loop bookkeeping; setup, planning, warmups, result formatting and cleanup are excluded.
method.counter_interpretation: instructions:u and cycles:u count user-mode work only. CPU is the captured task-clock:u divided by nine, not a per-sample CPU measurement. User CPI is cycles:u / instructions:u. Software diagnostics retain their :u qualifiers; they are not proof of zero scheduler activity. No CPU frequency is inferred.
method.cpu_tick_scope: /proc/stat CPU 2 and SMT sibling CPU 10 snapshots span the whole subprocess, not only the enabled counter window. They are circumstantial activity diagnostics.
method.summary: Means include all samples. Pooled medians use all 72 samples per variant and case. Counter means divide each process total by nine. No samples or processes are discarded.
method.historical_limit: Arithmetic and filter sources and candidate lockfile match decimal-normalized-performance.json. Exact-case selection and perf control relink both benchmark binaries and skip other suite queries. These are new binary hashes and execution contexts, not exact historical binary reproductions.

validation.reason: No arithmetic or dependency changes. Both candidates match their reviewed source hashes; the harness validates selected controls and row/NULL counts.

conclusion.observation: This targeted run does not reproduce consistently slower after-version execution in these three cases. Instruction counts are effectively unchanged. The narrow NULL case retains a +1.45% pooled mean elapsed increase; the mixed literal mean decreases 2.72%.
conclusion.same_binary_variance: before-6-mixed_literal is slower than other runs of the identical before binary: mean 347.64 ms vs 286.04 ms in before-1, with unchanged instructions, increased task-clock and user CPI. after-6-narrow_null also slows on unchanged instructions.
conclusion.limits: Counters narrow the observed slowdowns to time spent executing essentially the same user instruction count, but do not isolate hardware, allocator, kernel, code-layout or interference causes. Historical anomalies remain unresolved; no global zero-regression or whole-query speed claim.
